summary: The article examines how financial institutions navigate overlapping cybersecurity regulations by adopting frameworks such as the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, ISO/IEC 27001 and the FSSCC Cybersecurity Profile. It covers new SEC disclosure rules, the role of AI and automation, employee training, continuous improvement and information sharing, with quotes from industry figures. It concludes that institutions must balance compliance with business objectives.
one_line: Financial firms use cybersecurity frameworks like NIST and ISO 27001, plus technology, training and information sharing, to manage complex and overlapping regulatory compliance demands.
key_facts: On November 15, 2023, the SEC under Chairman Gregory T. Simmons introduced a rigorous set of cybersecurity disclosure rules for financial firms.
James Schultz, chief compliance officer at Manhattan-based hedge fund Highwater Capital, said on December 6 that regulators have overlapping and sometimes conflicting requirements.
Prevalent frameworks used by firms include the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, ISO/IEC 27001, and the Financial Services Sector Coordinating Council's (FSSCC) Cybersecurity Profile.
The NIST Cybersecurity Framework outlines five key functions: Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, and Recover.
Maria Lopez, Head of Cybersecurity at Bancorp South, said on January 22, 2024 that the NIST framework aligns well with controls from the SEC, FDIC, and FINRA.
Dan Thompson, CISO of a mid-sized bank in Ohio, said NIST gave a language to bridge the gap between the IT team and the board (interview March 3, 2024).
ISO/IEC 27001 prescribes a management system for information security, and organizations meeting it can be certified.
Elena Rios of Aegis Firm International said on February 14, 2024 that ISO 27001 certification is a trust factor that crosses geographies.

Greg Masters, CEO of fintech startup DataSafe, said at TechFin Expo on April 19, 2024 that compliance cannot be achieved by manual means alone and AI-driven platforms are the new guardians of financial data.
On May 30, 2024, an alert employee at New York's United Bank first detected irregularities during a breach, helping thwart a potentially catastrophic cyber heist.
Sophia Nguyen of Red Shield said at the CyberSecure 2024 Summit on July 11 that compliance is a journey, not a destination.
An information-sharing hub, a partnership between major banks and regulatory authorities for exchanging threat intelligence, was announced on September 12, 2024.
Michael Chen said at the Global Cyber Finance Summit on October 4 that information sharing significantly enhances collective defense.
